div.head: ECf retr Rb XLIII
div.ab: Quod nullus animal uiuum uel pannum usatum emeret siue aliud sine plegiis et bonis testibus, opus quoque aureum uel argenteum absque aurifabris uel monetariis.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 672 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.

This is one of the chapter headings (rubrics) that a later writer, whom Liebermann calls “Rubricator II” and dates 1163–1189, made for the Retractator’s text; so the date given for ECf retr (c. 1140–59) does not apply to it. Liebermann prints them on pp. 670–672 as an appendix (Anhang) to ECf retr; they are numbered here “Rb” with his Roman numerals. He prints in small type what is taken from the text of ECf retr, so the words in bold are the Rubricator’s own.
Liebermann gives in the margin, in square brackets, the chapter of ECf retr that this heading belongs to: 38.

note.seg: opusque instead of o. q. Hv

div.ab: That no one should buy a live animal or used cloth or anything else without pledges and good witnesses, nor work of gold or silver without goldsmiths or moneyers.
